battle.title: Big-O Bounty Hunt
battle.description: Count loop steps and spot growth rates to claim the bounty.

questions.text: You double the input size and the running time of a program roughly quadruples. Which growth rate is most likely?
questions.explanation: Doubling n in a quadratic algorithm gives (2n)^2 = 4n^2, four times the work. Linear time would only double, and exponential time would grow far more than four times.
For i = 0..4 the inner loop runs 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 times, so count is 15, which is n(n+1)/2 for n = 5. 25 would be the count if j always started at 0.
i takes the values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 inside the loop (7 iterations) and the last doubling leaves i at 128. Doubling each pass is why such loops are O(log n), not O(n).

questions.text: A program must answer 100,000 queries of the form 'is this id stored?' against 100,000 stored ids. Which design gives the best total time?
options: Scan an ArrayList for every query
Sort the list again before every query, then binary search
Traverse a linked list for every query
Load the ids into a HashSet once and call contains for each query
questions.answer: Load the ids into a HashSet once and call contains for each query
questions.explanation: A HashSet gives about O(1) per lookup, so total work is about O(n). Scanning a list per query is O(n) each, O(n^2) overall, and re-sorting before every query is even slower.

questions.text: An outer loop runs n times. Inside it, j starts at 1 and doubles until it reaches n. What is the total time complexity?
questions.explanation: The inner loop runs about log2(n) times per outer iteration, and the outer loop repeats that n times, so the total is n * log n. Treating any inner loop as n steps gives the tempting but wrong O(n^2).
